about.title: Corning Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall cases in Corning often happen at the same kinds of places locals pass through every day — the gas stations and retail lots along I-5, small shops on Marguerite Avenue, or apartment walkways that go unrepaired for months. What separates a real premises liability claim from a simple accident is proof: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the spill, broken step, or icy patch, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? California gives you generally two years to bring a claim, though claims against a public entity (like a city-owned sidewalk or building) move on a much shorter clock. Because store and apartment surveillance footage is often erased within days or weeks, getting the right documentation started early matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened, explain your options, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, complaint records, and inspection history to build that case.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Corning businesses overwrite security footage within days. An attorney can move quickly to send a preservation request before the video showing what actually happened is gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Into Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so if you're found partly responsible for the fall, your recovery can be reduced by that percentage. Having someone push back on unfair blame-shifting protects the value of your claim.

items.question: I fell at a store near I-5 in Corning but didn't report it right away — is it too late?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally gives you two years from the date of the fall to bring a premises liability claim, though claims involving a government-owned property have a much shorter deadline. The sooner you connect with an attorney, though, the better the chance of preserving video and witness statements before they disappear.

items.question: What if the store says I was watching my phone and not looking where I walked?
items.answer: That's a common argument, and under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly at fault can reduce your recovery rather than eliminate it entirely. An attorney can evaluate the specific facts, including lighting, signage, and whether the hazard was hidden or obvious, to push back on an unfair fault split.
